# Decision memo: Route C reminder pilot

**To:** Operations lead  
**Decision:** Consider a limited extension only after the pilot dates, delivery record, accessibility gaps, and resources are checked. Do not treat the draft extension or calendar title as approval. This is a decision to investigate an extension, not a recommendation to scale the reminders beyond the tested population. [1][3][4][5][6]

The pilot log dates the reminder pilot **August 17–September 13, 2026**, on **Route C weekday trips only**. It covered **480 of 1,600 eligible weekday bookings (30%)**; the other 1,120 bookings were outside the reported pilot coverage. A coordinator excerpt instead says the pilot ended **September 12**. Use the log's September 13 end date provisionally, but mark it disputed and reconcile it against raw send logs before publication. The September 30 follow-up is a planned decision meeting: its calendar title says “extension approved,” while its details say the decision is pending. Treat approval as pending, not granted. [1][5][6]

Among the 480 covered bookings, reminders were delivered for **312/480 (65%)**. **74/312 (23.7%)** bookings in the delivered group were later cancelled, versus **31/168 (18.5%)** among bookings with no delivered reminder. The latter 168 include **53 missing phone numbers** and **115 carrier rejects**. In the preceding four weeks, **128/600 (21.3%)** Route C weekday bookings were cancelled. These are descriptive rates with different denominators, not evidence that reminders changed cancellation behavior: the baseline did not control for booking mix or disruptions, and delivered versus undelivered bookings were not randomized in the supplied record. [1][2]

An opt-out suppressed subsequent reminders within 24 hours; **the number of opt-outs was not recorded**. Preserve that suppression rule in any extension, but do not infer an opt-out rate or assume the policy was met for every case without checking records. English was the only text language; screen-reader wording review and Spanish translation remain unfinished, and no participant accessibility study is reported. These gaps limit readiness for a broader rollout. [1][3]

The six-week extension is only a **draft proposal**: it estimates **$1,200 in message fees and 12 staff hours per week**, with neither funding nor assignments approved. Before a September 30 decision, make two checks: **(1) proposed owner Nora, Operations lead:** reconcile end date, delivery failures, and suppression timing against raw send logs; **(2) proposed owner Ivo, Access lead:** complete the screen-reader wording review and Spanish translation assessment, then report remaining gaps. # Decision memo: Cedar Transit reminder pilot
**To:** Operations lead

## Recommendation
Conditionally support a six-week extension only after confirming the reporting dates, resolving delivery and access readiness, and approving funding and staffing. Do not treat the extension as authorized: source 4 is a draft with neither funding nor assignments approved; the calendar’s “extension approved” title is stale, while its details say decision pending. The planned decision meeting is September 30. [4–6]

## Evidence and limits
The pilot log records August 17–September 13, 2026, on Route C weekday trips only. Coverage was 480/1,600 eligible weekday bookings (30.0%); findings should not be generalized to all eligible bookings, other routes, or weekends. The coordinator instead reports a September 12 end date. Retain the log’s dates as provisional, explicitly flag the conflict, and reconcile against raw send logs before publication. [1,6]

Reminders reached 312/480 covered bookings (65.0%). Later cancellations were 74/312 (23.7%) among bookings with delivered reminders and 31/168 (18.5%) among those without delivered reminders. # Decision memo: Cedar Transit Route C reminder pilot
**To:** Operations lead  
**Decision:** Proceed only with a time-limited extension if the date discrepancy is reconciled, accessibility and language work is completed, and funding and staffing are explicitly approved. The supplied record supports further evaluation, not a claim that reminders caused fewer cancellations.

The pilot log records operation August 17–September 13, 2026, on Route C weekday trips only. It covered 480 of 1,600 eligible weekday bookings (30%); this is not evidence about other routes, weekends, or the uncovered 1,120 bookings. Of 312 bookings with a delivered reminder, 74 were later cancelled (23.7%). Among 168 bookings without a delivered reminder, 31 were later cancelled (18.5%). The log also records 53 delivery failures due to missing phone numbers and 115 carrier rejects. (1)

For comparison, the preceding four weeks had 128 cancellations among 600 Route C weekday bookings (21.3%). Booking mix and disruptions were uncontrolled, and the groups are not shown to be comparable, so neither a causal effect nor a reliable performance change can be inferred. (1–2)
